appraisal_events.evidence: prenait-elle l'habitude de ne plus craindre de lui déplaire et même de l'irriter et lui refusait-elle, quand cela lui était commode, les faveurs auxquelles il tenait le plus
appraisal_events.explanation: As the counterpart to Swann's reported submission, Odette is depicted as gaining confidence and freedom in the relationship, no longer fearing his displeasure and able to withhold what he wants most.

status_effects.explanation: Odette accrues relational leverage over Swann: certain of his return, she loses any fear of displeasing him and freely refuses him favors he most wants.

ambiguities: Forcheville is named only inside Swann's hedged, conditional self-reassurance ('s'il arrivait que Forcheville pensât à lui...', 'Si Forcheville et elle triomphaient...') about how Forcheville might regard him and would have to 'céder la place' to him at Odette's. Because this is entirely hypothetical interior reasoning by a jealous Swann trying to talk himself into a course of action, rather than a reported event or stable narrative claim, it was judged too speculative to score as a status effect for Forcheville.
